steps.title: Your hero is a behaviour too
steps.body: The character the player plays is a built-in behaviour, Hero: it walks, jumps, hits, is hurt and gains experience, and a behaviour of your own can change each of those decisions. First, a hero to play: in the Scene's Starter pack, Play as Rook.

steps.title: Read about Hero
steps.body: In Logic, under Built-in, press Hero (☺ marks a character's built-ins). Its fields are the sheet (hearts, speed, jump, strength…); its hooks are canJump, moveSpeed, hitPower, takeDamage and gainXp.

steps.title: Out of breath
steps.body: Press Extend and write canJump: three jumps close together and the hero is out of breath until it rests two seconds (time.now() is the game's clock). Delete the other hooks, or keep them: super gives the engine's answer.

code: most = field.number(3, { label: "Jumps before a rest", min: 1, max: 10 });

steps.title: Put it on Rook
steps.body: In Characters, open Rook's Behaviour tab and attach My Hero with + Script. The tab also shows Hero (built-in) with Rook's sheet as fields.

steps.title: A higher jump
steps.body: In the Hero row, set Jump to 1.5: the same setting as the Stats tab.

steps.title: Jump, jump, jump
steps.body: Press Play and press Space four times quickly: three high jumps, then the Console says Out of breath! and the hero stays down. Wait two seconds and it can jump again.
steps.task: Press Play and jump four times.

steps.title: Done!
steps.body: Your hero's decisions are yours now. moveSpeed (faster in water, slower when hurt), hitPower (a strong first hit), takeDamage (a shield that blocks one hit in three), gainXp (double experience at night). Neighbours are built-ins too: Neighbour.canTalk, and Damageable.takeDamage for ones that can be hurt.
